source_text: In hoc igitur loco hic sensus, quantum spectat ad historiam continetur, ut Deus loquatur ad populum: Quia nec odio vos in captivitatem tradidi, nec nunc oblivione iudicii de vinculis Babylonicae captivitatis exemi; sed ego, quantum in me est, paratus iugi vos benevolentia confovere, iustitiae meae tamen debui, ut et delinquentes hostibus traderem, et recrearem liberaremque vexatos. Sicut enim rusticandi gnarus non semper uno imminet operi, ut solis findat arva dentalibus; sed diverso genere votivae fertilitati rura componit; ita etiam ego dispensationum vices vario, ut tum pressuris, tum consolationibus voluntatem vestram frugibus possim aptare iustitiae. Denique, ut intellegatis quanta aequitate agam vobiscum, possem mussitationes vestras pro potestate despicere, ut sicut figulo figmentum suum dicere non potest: Quid fecisti? Ita etiam vobis silentii pondus imponerem; tamen contra haec exempla provoco vos, ut pro filiis meis et filiabus, id est, pro vobis et operibus manuum mearum me interrogetis, et discatis, totum me iuste, nec quidquam umquam fecisse crudeliter.
pass_a_gloss: In this place therefore this sense, as much as looks to history, is contained, that God speak to the people: Because neither by hatred did I hand you over into captivity, nor now by forgetfulness of judgment have I taken you out from the bonds of the Babylonian captivity; but I, as much as is in me, prepared to warm you with a yoked benevolence, nevertheless I owed to my justice, that I both hand over those offending to enemies, and recreate and free those vexed. For as one knowing farming does not always hang upon one work, that he split the fields with plow-teeth alone; but by a diverse kind he composes the countryside for vowed fertility; so also I vary the turns of dispensations, that now by pressures, now by consolations I may be able to fit your will to the fruits of justice. Finally, that you may understand with how great equity I act with you, I could despise your mutterings according to power, that as to a potter his thing fashioned cannot say: What have you done? so also I would impose the weight of silence on you; nevertheless against these examples I provoke you, that for my sons and daughters, that is, for you and the works of my hands you ask me, and you learn, that I have done the whole justly, nor anything ever cruelly.

lemmas.lexica: LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: In its historical meaning, then, this passage contains the following sense, as God speaks to the people: “I did not hand you over to captivity out of hatred, nor have I now released you from the bonds of Babylonian captivity through forgetfulness of judgment. As far as it lay with me, I was ready to cherish you with constant goodwill, but I owed it to my justice both to hand over sinners to their enemies and to restore and free those who had suffered. Someone skilled in farming does not always devote himself to one task, merely breaking the fields with the plowshare; he prepares the land in different ways for the fruitfulness he desires (Isaiah 28:24–29). So I too vary the turns of my dealings, so that by distress at one time and comfort at another I may fit your will for the fruits of righteousness.

To make you understand how fairly I deal with you, I could disregard your complaints on the strength of my power: just as something molded cannot say to its potter, ‘What have you done?’, I could impose the weight of silence on you. Nevertheless, contrary to these examples, I invite you to question me about my sons and daughters, that is, yourselves and the works of my hands, and to learn that I have done everything justly and never anything cruelly.”
